text:
The Avalanche are learning what a season without Nathan MacKinnon feels like. A lower-body injury that first looked manageable turned into a setback; Jared Bednar said he saw a specialist and it "wasn't quite that simple," and the estimated return is now Feb. 13. That's three months without the player who had 30 points in 20 games. In the three games since, Brock Nelson has taken his spot between Martin Necas and Artturi Lehkonen and Nicolas Roy's minutes have jumped from 12 a night to 16. The better news: Cale Makar, on injured reserve, has been taking regular reps beside Brett Kulak in a full-contact jersey, and was on the top power-play unit at practice.

Colorado has handled it better than you'd fear. The Avalanche are 3-1-1 in their last five with 54% of the expected goals (the quality of chances), and they come in rested after a 4-0 win over Anaheim six days ago, a 25-save shutout for Scott Wedgewood. Mackenzie Blackwood is projected to start. Nazem Kadri has gone seven games without a goal on 3.9 expected. Our sleeper is Devon Toews, 55% for a point with more ice time and a power-play role in Makar's absence.

Montreal's week was about Dylan Larkin. The Canadiens finally got him from Detroit on Sunday, sending Kirby Dach, Sam Montembeault, Michael Hage and picks, and Larkin's debut on Monday was a 2-1 loss to Los Angeles. He's on the first power-play unit already, which matters for a group missing Ivan Demidov, Mike Matheson, Josh Anderson and Chris Kreider. Jacob Fowler has been the steadiest thing about this team: .918 and 12.4 goals saved above expected. Juraj Slafkovský has 3 points in ten games on 7.6 expected and is two points from 200 for his career.

Our numbers have Colorado at 3.45 expected goals and Montreal at 2.88. Watch the penalty box: the Habs take 4.5 penalties a game, and Colorado's power play creates 0.80 expected goals a night.
headline: No MacKinnon for months, and Larkin's second game as a Hab
